To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) part-to-image matching is the dominant cost of object detection with part-based models, 2) this can be accelerated by a coarse-to-fine procedure, and 3) a combination of coarse-to-fine and cascade-of-parts yields very significant speedups.
the cost of matching parts to the image dominates the cost of detection, and that a coarse-to-fine hierarchical approach can be used to minimize this cost.

(a) the computational bottleneck of detection with part based methods lies in the part-to-image comparisons, not in the optimization, and that (b) a coarse-to-fine strategy can be used to reduce the cost of part-to-image comparison by a large factor, with little loss in accuracy.

The main takeaway from our work is that

, when using deformable part based models, the cost of computing a single optimal configuration is relatively low compared to the cost of computing all possible part configurations, and therefore can be neglected in the overall detection cost.
the computational cost of detection is dominated by the number of part-image comparisons and not by the number of configurations.

the cost of computing a part based model is often dominated by the cost incurred by matching the model parts to the image, which suggests that a significant speedup in the detection process may be achieved by minimizing this cost.
